title: Geometric reducedness from the generic local rings
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ a reduced scheme over $k$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Suppose that for every generic point $\xi$ [def-sc-generic-point] of every irreducible component of $X$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], and every field extension $L/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], the commutative ring $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}\otimes_k L$ is reduced (has no nonzero nilpotent element). Here $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ is the stalk of the structure sheaf at $\xi$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], namely the ring of germs of sections on open neighbourhoods of $\xi$, and the tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] has multiplication $(a\otimes l)(b\otimes m)=ab\otimes lm$. Then $X$ is geometrically reduced over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]: $X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L$ is reduced for every field extension $L/k$ (the fibre product is as in [def-pc-fibre-product]). No finiteness assumption on $X$ or its set of irreducible components is imposed.

proof.text: Fix a field extension $L/k$ and an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $X$. By [def-pc-reduced-scheme], $A$ is reduced. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], the closure of a minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ in $U$ is the irreducible closed set $V(\mathfrak p)$, and any irreducible closed set containing it is $V(\mathfrak q)$ with $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$, hence equals it by minimality. Its closure $C$ in $X$ is an irreducible component: if an irreducible subset $Y$ contains $C$, then $Y\cap U$ is a nonempty open subset of $Y$. Any two nonempty opens of $Y\cap U$ intersect because they are nonempty opens of $Y$; every nonempty open of $Y$ meets $Y\cap U$, so $Y\cap U$ is dense in $Y$. Its closure in $U$ is therefore irreducible and contains $V(\mathfrak p)$, hence equals $V(\mathfrak p)$. Consequently $Y\subseteq\overline{Y\cap U}^{X}\subseteq C$, proving maximality. The point $\xi$ represented by $\mathfrak p$ has closure $C$, so it is generic in this global component [def-sc-generic-point]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization](c), the germ map identifies $A_{\mathfrak p}$ with $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ as an $A$-algebra and hence as a $k$-algebra. Tensoring this isomorphism and its inverse with $L$ gives inverse ring maps, so the hypothesis says $A_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_k L$ is reduced for every minimal prime $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 04KS(3), reduction to affine generic local rings; Tag 035W, local-ring interpretation

proof.text: The maps $A\to A_{\mathfrak p}$ jointly detect zero. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field] gives $\mathfrak p A_{\mathfrak p}=0$. The kernel of $A\to A_{\mathfrak p}$ is exactly $\mathfrak p$: one inclusion follows from this equality; for the other, if $a/1=0$, then $sa=0$ for some $s\notin\mathfrak p$, and primality gives $a\in\mathfrak p$. If $a$ vanishes in all these localizations, it belongs to every minimal prime. Every prime contains a minimal prime by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] with $I=0$, so $a$ lies in every prime. By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] with $I=0$, $a$ is nilpotent, hence zero because $A$ is reduced.

The induced maps $A\otimes_k L\to A_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_k L$ also jointly detect zero, without any finiteness of the set of primes. Write an element $z$ as $\sum_{j=1}^r a_j\otimes e_j$ with $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ linearly independent over $k$: choose a basis of the finite-dimensional span of the finitely many coefficients of any tensor expression and collect coefficients. By [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector], extend these independent vectors to a vector-space basis of $L$ and let $\lambda_j:L\to k$ be the coordinate linear functionals. If every image of $z$ is zero, applying $\operatorname{id}\otimes\lambda_j$ gives $a_j/1=0$ in every $A_{\mathfrak p}$. Step 2 gives $a_j=0$ for all $j$, so $z=0$. If $z$ is nilpotent, each image is nilpotent in the reduced ring from step 1 and is therefore zero. Joint detection gives $z=0$, proving $A\otimes_k L$ reduced.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] with base ring $k$ and $k$-algebras $A,L$, $U_L$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_k L)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] it is an open subscheme of $X_L$. It is precisely the inverse image of $U$: a morphism to $X_L$ whose composite to $X$ factors through $U$ factors uniquely through $U_L$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The inverse images of the affine opens of $X$ therefore cover $X_L$. All their rings are reduced by step 3, and all their stalks are reduced: if $(b/s)^d=0$ in a localization of a reduced ring, then $tb^d=0$ for a denominator $t$, so $(tb)^d=0$, whence $tb=0$ and $b/s=0$. Each point of $X_L$ lies in one such affine chart; [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization](c), applied to this chart in $X_L$, identifies its local ring with the localization of its reduced section ring at the corresponding prime. Thus [def-pc-reduced-scheme] makes $X_L$ reduced. Since $L/k$ was arbitrary, [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] gives geometric reducedness of $X$. The empty scheme satisfies the same argument vacuously.
